Within the text block a brace diagram in the upper part (Noxgrammatical/Doctrina tradita & praedicata, with braces and the word "per ipsum" at the right), then a second brace diagram (Doctrina tradita est: Generalis & communis / Particularis), then running paragraphs. main_text.p: i. animæ & corporis separatione. Gen. 5.24. Heb. 11. 5. 2. Reg. 2.9.
main_text.l: Doctrina tradita est { Generalis & communis, sed clarius prædicata. { Particularis, hominibus eius ætatis.
main_text.p: Generalis, erat prædicatio doctrinæ, de gratuito fœdere, ut secundum homines i. carne, damnarentur: Secundum Deum, i. spiritu, viverent in æternum.

Particularis de utroq; fœdere, erga improbos erat, diluuij in omnium viuetium interitum, etiam in improbos (nisi fide in Christo recipiscant) æternum, denunciatio. Gen. 3.6.11.12.13. De fidelibus erat, Deum fœdus singulare, & gratuitum, erga genus humanum, in Noæ familia pepegisse, ipsos fore per fidem iustitiæ Christi hæredes: quod mirifica illa omnium viuetium, (quod ad genera & species attinet,) liberatione à diluuio obsignabat. Gen. 6.18.21. & 22. Heb. 11.7.
Sacramentum administratum, erat (a) sacramentum extraordinarium primum, siue initiationis, qua ex arcæ structura, particularem doctrinam ex utraq; parte obsignauit. (a) 1. Pet. 3.21. Heb. 11.7. Eius

page.notes: Marginal and brace labels are partly illegible in the scan; the diagram lines are reproduced as best read. The Greek words in the first diagram (Noxχρημαλιστ, θέντος) are uncertain and may be misprinted. The right-edge note "Eius" is a catchword-like word at the foot right and is treated as a note.
